title: Toast
lede: A succinct message that is displayed temporarily.

examples.description: One default toast at rest: 420px wide (at most the viewport less two gaps), a 12px radius, the menu shadow, 16px padding, 21px line height, the dismiss control at the end of the row.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Success toast
examples.description: The success toast: a blue-700 fill with the contrast foreground, the type read to assistive tech before the message.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible type="success" />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Warning toast
examples.description: The warning toast: an amber-800 fill with the gray-1000 foreground.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible type="warning" />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Error toast
examples.description: The error toast: a red-800 fill with the contrast foreground, the type read to assistive tech before the message.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible type="error" />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Action and cancel
examples.description: A toast with an action: the message row loses its dismiss control and a row of two small buttons follows it, the cancel action (Dismiss unless named) as a tertiary button and the action as a default one; the toast is an alert dialog labelled by its message.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible action="Undo" cancelAction="Cancel" />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Error action
examples.description: The action row on an error toast: the cancel button takes the contrast foreground.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible type="error" action="Undo" />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Warning action
examples.description: The action row on a warning toast: the cancel button takes the gray-1000 foreground.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible type="warning" action="Undo" />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Undo control
examples.description: An undo handler adds a square tertiary undo button before the dismiss control.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible onUndoAction={undo} />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Without close
examples.description: hideX drops the dismiss control and the message spans the row.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible hideX />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Visual
examples.description: A visual block (128px unless sized) bleeds to the toast's edges above the message, and the toast clips its content.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible visual={<Cover />} />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Full bleed visual
examples.description: fullBleed drops the toast's padding: the visual reaches its edges and the message row sits flush.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible fullBleed visual={<Cover />} />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Centered
examples.description: The centered viewport: the area sits at calc(50% - 210px) from the right, half a toast's width.
examples.code:
<Toasts center>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Stack
examples.description: Three toasts: the area rises 10px, the front toast (the newest, last in the DOM) shows in full, the ones behind it collapse to 50px, translate up 20px per step behind the front toast's height and scale down 5% per step; the message of a toast behind the front fades out. A fourth would be hidden (a third on a viewport of 400px or less).
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="Domain added" visible />
  <Toast text="Project archived" visible />
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Stack expanded
examples.description: The pointer over the area expands the stack: every toast takes its own height again, moves up by the heights in front of it plus 20px per step at full scale, shows its message, and grows a 20px bridge below it so the pointer can travel between toasts.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="Domain added" visible />
  <Toast text="Project archived" visible />
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Entering
examples.description: A toast just mounted: transparent, translated a full height down and 150px back, before the 350ms entry transition.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.

examples.heading: Leaving
examples.description: A toast on its way out: transparent and scaled to 0.98 over 160ms, then removed.
examples.code:
<Toasts>
  <Toast text="The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence." visible hiding />
</Toasts>

children.text: The Evil Rabbit jumped over the fence.
